For children aged 1 to 10 years or children over 10 years but weighing less than 40 kg, the recommended dosage is 5 mg/kg orally once daily or every 12 hours, not exceeding a maximum of 150 mg per day. 2. For children over 10 years of age and weighing more than 40 kg, the recommended dosage is 100 mg orally every 12 hours. 3. In cases of severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance <10 mL/min) or liver impairment, the medication should be administered once daily. 4. Rimantadine interacts with several drugs and substances through pharmacodynamic synergism, which may enhance central nervous system (CNS) side effects. These include aclidinium, atropine (IV/IM), glycopyrrolate (inhaled), henbane, hyoscyamine spray, oxybutynin (oral and transdermal), and rapacuronium. Caution and close monitoring are advised when these combinations are used. 5. Ublituximab may decrease the effects of rimantadine due to its immunosuppressive properties, increasing the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Rimantadine increases the effects of aclidinium, atropine (IV/IM), glycopyrrolate (inhaled), henbane, hyoscyamine spray, oxybutynin (oral and transdermal), and rapacuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of these interactions is considered minor or unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 7. Common side effects of rimantadine include dizziness (2%), nervousness (1-2%), fatigue (1%), headache (1%), insomnia (2%), difficulty concentrating (<2%), anxiety (1%), anorexia (2%), weakness (1%), nausea (3%), vomiting (2%), xerostomia (2%), and abdominal pain (1%). 8. Rare but serious side effects include dyspnea, agitation, ataxia, tachycardia, tremor, convulsions, heart block, hyperkinesias, bronchospasm, gait abnormalities, and hypersensitivity reactions to amantadine, rimantadine, or any drug component. 9. The CDC advises against the use of rimantadine for the treatment or prophylaxis of influenza in the United States during the 2008-09 influenza season. 10. Caution is advised in patients with a history of seizures, and the medication should be discontinued if seizures occur. 11. Rimantadine should be avoided in patients with active or uncontrolled psychosis. 12. Use caution in patients with renal impairment. 13. Rimantadine is classified as Pregnancy Category C, indicating that risk to the fetus cannot be ruled out. It also enters breast milk, so caution is advised during lactation. 14. Rimantadine inhibits the replication of three subtypes of influenza A (H1N1, H2N2, H3N2) early in the viral replication cycle but has no activity against influenza B virus. 15. The half-life of rimantadine is approximately 4 hours but may be prolonged in elderly patients and those with severe renal or hepatic impairment. 16. The peak plasma concentration is reached approximately 6 hours after administration. 17. Rimantadine is primarily excreted in the urine, with less than 25% excreted as unchanged drug. Hemodialysis does not significantly contribute to its clearance. 18. The information provided is for general informational and educational purposes only. Individual plans and formulary information may vary, and it is recommended to contact the applicable plan provider for the most current information. 19.
